title: Kanda Poha
description: Flattened rice cooked with onion, peanuts and turmeric.
steps: Rinse poha in a colander until soft but not mushy; drain, sprinkle salt, sugar and turmeric and set aside 5 minutes.
Heat oil, fry peanuts until golden and remove.
Add mustard seeds; when they pop add curry leaves, green chilli and onion. Cook until onion is soft.
Add the poha, mix gently and cook covered on low heat for 3 minutes.
Stir in peanuts, lemon juice and coriander. Serve warm.

title: Rava Upma
description: Savoury semolina porridge tempered with mustard and curry leaves.
steps: Dry roast rava on low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until fragrant; set aside.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and urad dal until golden.
Add curry leaves, chilli, ginger and onion; cook until onion softens.
Add water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower heat, add rava in a thin stream while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cover and cook 2 minutes, rest 2 minutes, then fluff and serve.

title: Idli
description: Soft steamed rice and urad dal cakes (uses ready fermented batter).
steps: Grease the idli moulds lightly with oil.
Stir the batter gently; add salt only if it was not salted before fermenting.
Fill each mould about three quarters full.
Steam on medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Rest 2 minutes, unmould with a wet spoon and serve with chutney or sambar.

title: Plain Dosa with Potato Masala
description: Crisp rice and dal crepe filled with spiced potato.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, chilli and onion; cook until soft.
Add turmeric, salt and the mashed boiled potatoes with a splash of water; mix and set aside.
Heat a flat tawa, wipe with oil and pour a ladle of batter, spreading in a thin circle.
Drizzle a little oil around the edge and cook until golden and crisp.
Place potato masala in the centre, fold and serve hot.

title: Aloo Paratha
description: Whole wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potato.
steps: Knead flour with water and 0.5 tsp salt into a soft dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mash potatoes and mix with chilli, coriander, garam masala, chilli powder and remaining salt.
Roll a dough ball into a small circle, place filling in the centre, seal and flatten.
Roll gently into a paratha, dusting with flour as needed.
Cook on a hot tawa, brushing ghee on both sides until golden spots appear.

title: Moong Dal Chilla
description: Savoury lentil pancakes made from a quick soaked batter.
steps: Drain the dal and grind with chilli, ginger, cumin and a little water to a pourable batter.
Mix in salt, onion and coriander.
Spread a ladle of batter thinly on a hot greased tawa.
Cook until the underside is golden, drizzle oil, flip and cook the other side.
Serve with green chutney.

title: Tadka Toor Dal
description: Everyday yellow dal finished with a ghee and cumin tempering.
steps: Rinse dal and pressure cook with water, turmeric, tomato and salt for 4 whistles.
Mash the cooked dal lightly and add hot water if too thick; simmer 5 minutes.
Heat ghee, add cumin, then garlic, dry chillies and asafoetida until the garlic turns golden.
Add chilli powder off the heat and pour the tempering over the dal.
Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or roti.

title: Rajma Masala
description: Kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy, a North Indian favourite.
steps: Pressure cook soaked rajma with salt and 3 cups water for 6 to 7 whistles until very soft.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste for a minute, then tomato puree, coriander and chilli powder; cook until oil separates.
Add the cooked rajma with its liquid and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken.
Stir in garam masala and serve with rice.

title: Chole
description: Spiced chickpea curry with a tangy tomato base.
steps: Pressure cook chickpeas with salt, turmeric and the tea bag for 8 to 10 whistles until soft; discard the tea bag.
Heat oil, add cumin and onions; cook until deep golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomato puree, chilli powder and chole masala; cook until oil separates.
Add chickpeas with some cooking water and simmer 15 minutes.
Mash a few chickpeas to thicken; serve with bhature, roti or rice.

title: Palak Paneer
description: Paneer cubes in a smooth spiced spinach gravy.
steps: Blanch spinach with green chillies in boiling water for 2 minutes, then cool in cold water and blend to a smooth puree.
Heat oil, add cumin, onion and ginger-garlic paste; cook until golden.
Add tomato and salt and cook until soft.
Pour in the spinach puree and simmer 5 minutes without covering to keep the colour.
Add paneer and garam masala, simmer 3 minutes, finish with cream and serve.

title: Aloo Gobi
description: Dry potato and cauliflower sabzi with turmeric and cumin.
steps: Heat oil, add cumin and ginger, then onion; cook until light golden.
Add tomato and the powdered spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add potatoes, cauliflower and salt; mix well.
Cover and cook on low heat 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Uncover and cook 2 minutes to dry out; garnish with coriander.

title: Jeera Rice
description: Basmati rice flavoured with ghee-fried cumin.
steps: Rinse rice until the water runs clear and soak 20 minutes; drain.
Heat ghee, add cumin and bay leaf until the cumin sizzles.
Add the rice and fry gently for a minute.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, cover and cook on lowest heat for 12 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes covered, then fluff with a fork.

title: Vegetable Pulao
description: Fragrant one-pot rice with mixed vegetables and whole spices.
steps: Rinse and soak rice for 20 minutes; drain.
Heat ghee, add whole spices and onion; fry until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and vegetables; cook 3 minutes.
Add rice, water and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed; rest 5 minutes and fluff.

title: Curd Rice
description: Cooling South Indian rice mixed with yogurt and a light tempering.
steps: Mash the warm rice slightly and let it cool.
Mix in curd, milk and salt until creamy.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, urad dal until golden, then chilli, ginger and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the rice and mix.
Serve at room temperature or chilled with pickle.

title: Lemon Rice
description: Tangy turmeric rice with peanuts and curry leaves.
steps: Heat oil, add mustard seeds, chana dal and peanuts; fry until golden.
Add chillies, curry leaves and turmeric.
Add the rice and salt and toss gently on low heat for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in lemon juice.
Serve with papad or raita.

title: Phulka (Chapati)
description: Soft, puffed everyday whole wheat flatbread.
steps: Mix flour and salt, add water gradually and knead a soft dough; add oil and rest 20 minutes.
Divide into equal balls and roll each into a thin circle, dusting with flour.
Cook on a hot tawa for 20 seconds until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook the other side, then place directly on a flame (or press with a cloth) so it puffs.
Brush with ghee and keep covered.

title: Puri
description: Deep-fried puffed wheat bread served with potato sabzi.
steps: Mix flour, rava and salt, then knead a stiff dough with water; rest 20 minutes.
Roll small balls into 4 inch circles of even thickness.
Heat oil until a pinch of dough rises quickly.
Slide in a puri and press gently so it puffs; fry until golden on both sides.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

title: Methi Thepla
description: Gujarati fenugreek flatbread that keeps well for travel.
steps: Mix flour, methi, curd, spices, salt, sesame and 1 tbsp oil.
Knead a soft dough with a little water; rest 15 minutes.
Roll thin circles from small balls.
Cook on a hot tawa, brushing oil on both sides, until brown spots appear.
Serve with curd or pickle.

title: Aloo Samosa
description: Crisp pastry triangles filled with spiced potato and peas.
steps: Rub 4 tbsp oil and 0.5 tsp salt into the flour, knead a stiff dough with water and rest 30 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, add cumin, peas, chilli and spices; mix in the mashed potato and remaining salt for the filling. Cool.
Roll a ball into an oval, cut in half, shape each half into a cone, fill and seal the edge with water.
Fry on low-medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until golden and crisp.
Serve with green chutney.

title: Onion Pakora
description: Crunchy gram flour fritters, ideal with tea on a rainy day.
steps: Mix onions with salt and let sit 5 minutes to release water.
Add besan, chilli, ajwain, chilli powder and coriander; add just enough water to bind a thick batter.
Heat oil on medium.
Drop small spoonfuls into the oil and fry until golden and crisp, turning occasionally.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

title: Khaman Dhokla
description: Light, spongy steamed gram flour cake with a mustard tempering.
steps: Whisk besan, curd, water, paste, turmeric, sugar and salt into a smooth batter; rest 10 minutes.
Grease a plate and prepare a steamer.
Add Eno and 1 tbsp water, stir lightly once until frothy and pour immediately into the plate.
Steam covered for 12 to 15 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool, cut into squares and pour over a tempering of hot oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves.

title: Suji Halwa
description: Quick semolina pudding roasted in ghee with sugar and cardamom.
steps: Boil water with sugar and cardamom until the sugar dissolves; keep hot.
Heat ghee, fry cashews and raisins and set aside.
In the same ghee roast rava on low heat for 6 to 8 minutes until fragrant and light brown.
Carefully pour in the hot syrup (it will splutter) while stirring.
Cook until thick and the ghee leaves the sides; mix in cashews and raisins.

title: Rice Kheer
description: Creamy milk and rice pudding scented with cardamom.
steps: Rinse rice and soak for 20 minutes; drain.
Bring milk to a boil in a heavy pan, then add the rice.
Simmer on low heat for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick, until thick and the rice is very soft.
Add sugar and cardamom and cook 5 more minutes.
Stir in nuts and saffron; serve warm or chilled.

title: Coconut Chutney
description: Fresh coconut chutney to serve with idli and dosa.
steps: Grind coconut, chana dal, chilli, ginger and salt with water to a smooth chutney.
Transfer to a bowl.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves until they crackle.
Pour the tempering over the chutney and serve.

title: Coriander-Mint Chutney
description: Bright, tangy green chutney for samosa, pakora and sandwiches.
steps: Wash the herbs well.
Blend everything with the water to a smooth paste.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Store in the fridge and use within 3 days.

title: Masala Chai
description: Strong milk tea simmered with ginger and cardamom.
steps: Boil water with ginger and cardamom for 2 minutes.
Add tea leaves and simmer 1 minute.
Add milk and sugar and bring to a boil, watching it does not overflow.
Simmer 2 minutes for a deeper colour, then strain into cups.

title: Sweet Lassi
description: Thick, chilled yogurt drink with cardamom.
steps: Add curd, sugar, cardamom and cold water or milk to a blender.
Blend until frothy.
Pour over ice and serve immediately.

title: Nimbu Pani
description: Fresh salted lemonade, a summer cooler.
steps: Stir sugar and salt into cold water until dissolved.
Add lemon juice and cumin powder.
Crush the mint lightly and add.
Serve over ice.
